title: उत्तरपर्व · अध्याय १८५

items.text:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
आत्मप्रतिकृतिर्नाम यथोक्तं कस्यचित्पुरा ॥
तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि दानं मानविवर्धनम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
|| śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca || ||
ātmapratikṛtirnāma yathoktaṃ kasyacitpurā ||
tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānaṃ mānavivardhanam || 1 ||

items.text:
दानकालः सदा तस्य मुनिभिः परिकीर्तितः ॥
पुण्यैः पुण्यदिनं पार्थ प्राप्यते जीवितैर्न च ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
dānakālaḥ sadā tasya munibhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
puṇyaiḥ puṇyadinaṃ pārtha prāpyate jīvitairna ca || 2 ||

items.text:
लोहजां प्रकृतिं भव्यां कारयित्वात्मनो नृप ॥
अभीष्टवाहनगतामिष्टालंकारसंयुताम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
lohajāṃ prakṛtiṃ bhavyāṃ kārayitvātmano nṛpa ||
abhīṣṭavāhanagatāmiṣṭālaṃkārasaṃyutām || 3 ||

items.text:
कुंकुमेनानुलिप्तांगीं कर्पूरागुरुवासिताम् ॥
स्त्री चेद्ददाति शयने शयितां कारयेत्स्वयम् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
kuṃkumenānuliptāṃgīṃ karpūrāguruvāsitām ||
strī ceddadāti śayane śayitāṃ kārayetsvayam || 5 ||

items.text:
यद्यदिष्टतमं किंचित्तत्सर्वं पार्श्वतो न्यसेत् ॥
उपकारकरं स्त्रीणां स्वशरीरे च यद्भवेत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ kiṃcittatsarvaṃ pārśvato nyaset ||
upakārakaraṃ strīṇāṃ svaśarīre ca yadbhavet || 6 ||

items.text:
तत्सर्वं स्थापयेत्पार्श्वे स्वयं संचिंत्य चेतसि ॥
एतत्सर्वं मेलयित्वा स्वेस्वे स्थाने निधाय च ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tatsarvaṃ sthāpayetpārśve svayaṃ saṃciṃtya cetasi ||
etatsarvaṃ melayitvā svesve sthāne nidhāya ca || 7 ||

items.text:
पूजयित्वा लोकपालान्गृहान्देवीं विनायकम् ॥
तत शुक्लांबरः स्नात्वा गृहीतकुसुमांजलिः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
pūjayitvā lokapālāngṛhāndevīṃ vināyakam ||
tata śuklāṃbaraḥ snātvā gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
इममुच्चारयेन्मंत्रं विप्रस्य पुरतो बुधः ॥
आत्मनः प्रतिमा चेयं सर्वोपकरणैर्युता ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
imamuccārayenmaṃtraṃ viprasya purato budhaḥ ||
ātmanaḥ pratimā ceyaṃ sarvopakaraṇairyutā || 9 ||

items.text:
सर्वरत्नसमायुक्ता तव विप्र निवेदिता ॥
आत्मा शंभुः शिवः शौरिः शक्रः सुरगणैर्वृतः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
sarvaratnasamāyuktā tava vipra niveditā ||
ātmā śaṃbhuḥ śivaḥ śauriḥ śakraḥ suragaṇairvṛtaḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
तस्मादात्मप्रदानेन ममात्मा सुप्रसीदतु ॥
इत्युच्चार्य ततो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणाय युधिष्ठिर ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
tasmādātmapradānena mamātmā suprasīdatu ||
ityuccārya tato dadyādbrāhmaṇāya yudhiṣṭhira || 11 ||

items.text:
ब्राह्मणश्चापि गृह्णीयात्कोदादिति च कीर्तयन् ॥
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य प्रणिपत्य विसर्जयेत् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇaścāpi gṛhṇīyātkodāditi ca kīrtayan ||
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇipatya visarjayet || 12 ||

items.text:
विधिनानेन राजेन्द्र दानमेतत्प्रयच्छति ॥
यः पुमानथ वा नारी शृणुयात्फलमाप्नुयात् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
vidhinānena rājendra dānametatprayacchati ||
yaḥ pumānatha vā nārī śṛṇuyātphalamāpnuyāt || 13 ||

items.text:
साग्रं वर्षशतं दिव्यं स्वर्गलोके सुरैर्वृतः ॥
अभीष्टफलदानेन ह्यभीष्टफलभाग्भवेत् ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ divyaṃ svargaloke surairvṛtaḥ ||
abhīṣṭaphaladānena hyabhīṣṭaphalabhāgbhavet || 14 ||

items.text:
यत्रैवोत्पद्यते जंतुः प्राप्ते कर्मक्षये पुनः ॥
तत्रैव सर्वकामानां फलभाग्भवते नृपः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
yatraivotpadyate jaṃtuḥ prāpte karmakṣaye punaḥ ||
tatraiva sarvakāmānāṃ phalabhāgbhavate nṛpaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
इष्टबंधुजनैः सार्द्धं न वियोगं कदाचन ॥
प्राप्नोति पुरुषो राजन्स्वर्गे चानंत्यमश्नुते ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
iṣṭabaṃdhujanaiḥ sārddhaṃ na viyogaṃ kadācana ||
prāpnoti puruṣo rājansvarge cānaṃtyamaśnute || 16 ||

items.text:
यश्चात्मनः प्रतिकृतिं वरवाहनस्था हैमीं विधाय धनधान्यसमाकुलां च ॥
सोपस्करं द्विजवराय ददाति भक्त्या चंद्रार्कवत्स दिवि भाति हि राजराजः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
yaścātmanaḥ pratikṛtiṃ varavāhanasthā haimīṃ vidhāya dhanadhānyasamākulāṃ ca ||
sopaskaraṃ dvijavarāya dadāti bhaktyā caṃdrārkavatsa divi bhāti hi rājarājaḥ || 17 ||

items.h: इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवाद आत्मप्रतिकृतिदानविधिवर्णनं नाम पञ्चाशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ।। १८५ ।।

en_summary: Krishna gives the gift called the image of oneself (atma-pratikriti), which increases honour; the sages say its time is always, since a holy day comes by merit, not merely by living. A fine iron image of oneself is made, riding one's favourite mount, with one's favourite ornaments, in one's favourite world and with all its furnishings, covered with silk and fine cloth, adorned with jewels, anointed with saffron and scented with camphor and agaru; if a woman gives it, she has it made lying on a bed. Whatever one likes best, and whatever is useful to a woman for her own body, is set beside it, each in its place. After worshipping the world guardians, the planets, the Goddess and Vinayaka, the bathed patron, in white, holding flowers, says before the Brahmin: "This image of myself, with all its furnishings and all jewels, is offered to you, Brahmin; the Self is Shambhu, Shiva, Shauri and Indra with the gods; so by this gift of the self may my self be pleased." He gives it, the Brahmin accepts it with the "Ko 'dat" verse, and the patron walks around, bows and sends him off. A man or woman who gives this, or hears of it, lives in heaven among the gods for over a hundred divine years; giving what one most desires, one gains what one most desires. When the merit is spent and the person is born again, he enjoys every wish there, is never parted from loved ones and kin, and gains endless heaven. One who makes a gold image of himself on a fine mount, full of wealth and grain, and gives it with its furnishings to a good Brahmin, shines in heaven like the moon and sun, a king of kings.
